newsitem.title: USA: AES Corp/Ecology group bid for NEES plants.
newsitem.headline: AES Corp/Ecology group bid for NEES plants.

text.p: The environmental group Conservation Law Foundation (CLF) said Monday it had joined with AES Corp to bid for New England Electric System's 18 plants.
"It's probably a long shot, but a lot of the recent rumors are saying that the bids are dropping," CLF Director Douglas Foy told Reuters. "At this point, I guess it's anybody's guess."

Foy said the group had entered into the unusual alliance with AES, a Virginia power company, because it presented "the unique opportunity to close some of the dirtiest fossil-fuel plants in the region."
If its bid is successful, the alliance will close at least one and and as many as five of NEES's nine fossil fuel plants, Foy said.
He declined to say how much his group had bid for the plants. He also declined to specify which facilities it would seek to close, except to say that the oldest and dirtiest plants would be targeted.

The alliance was one of 25 groups that submitted non-binding bids for NEES's 18 non-nuclear power generating plants, which have a book value of $1.2 billion and are rated at nearly 4,000 megawatts of electricity.

NEES has invited fewer than 10 of the bidding groups to submit binding bids in late June as part of its efforts to separate its power plant business from its power distribution business, said Susan Stevens, a spokeswoman for NEES.
